ma_force_boulder_cluster_the.blurb: A compact group of sixteen boulder problems in the Mount Jacob section of the Tompson Street Reservation on Cape Ann, along Massachusetts' North Shore. A lot of variety is squeezed into a small footprint, so it works well for a quick evening session. Difficulty begins around V2 and reaches V7, with most problems sitting in the V3 to V4 range and a handful of V6 testpieces, which suits intermediate and strong boulderers better than complete beginners. The walk in is short, roughly five minutes on a path that drops downhill to the cluster.

ma_roadside_crag.blurb: This very small outcrop sits along Wendell Road near where Wendell meets Montague, at the northeastern edge of Montague State Forest in western Massachusetts. The cliff is visible from the car and reached in well under a minute. It holds about ten boulder problems, most around V4 with a few easier and harder ones, plus five short sport routes running from 5.9 into the 5.11 range, mainly 5.10. Holds are plentiful, so linking moves and variations is part of the fun. It sits mostly in shade, making it a convenient after-work stop, a fair choice for kids, or an overflow option when busier crags nearby are packed.
ma_roadside_crag.parking_note: Small pull-off lot on Wendell Road, just up the hill and around the bend when driving east from Millers Falls past Mormon Hollow Road. Room for a few cars.
ma_roadside_crag.approach: A short, obvious path leads from the lot to the cliff in under a minute.

ma_barrel_boulder.blurb: One of the main problem-rich blocks at Rocky Pond in Boylston, central Massachusetts, roughly a quarter hour from Worcester. This granite boulder offers fifteen problems in a wide mix of styles: a roof crack, a technical slab, a chimney, a stemming scoop, lip traverses and an overhanging prow. Most problems fall between V1 and V4, but there is a cluster at V7 and a couple of very hard lines at V9 and above, with more projects still unclimbed. The walk takes several minutes along a cut through the woods, finishing with a steep climb up and a drop down on the far side.
ma_barrel_boulder.approach: Follow the main trail from the parking area for about six or seven minutes along the wide cut through the woods. Where it bends right and climbs a steep hill, go up, then keep left and descend; the boulder appears on the left at the bottom.

ma_playground_the.blurb: A short granite crag in the Rattlesnake Rocks group in the Blue Hills near Braintree, south of Boston. Fifteen climbs, split about evenly between trad and top rope, run from scrambly easy terrain up to the 5.11 range, though most sit in the 5.7 to 5.9 band, making it a reasonable place for newer leaders and top-rope sessions. The cliff is low, with an overhanging roof section toward the right side, and it sits in fairly dense forest where it can be hard to spot at first. Trees along the top are handy for building anchors.
ma_playground_the.parking_note: Pull off on the north side of Wampatuck Road, beyond the Bunker Hill Quarry.
ma_playground_the.approach: Walk back east along the road to a dirt track on a raised embankment above a pipeline, then follow faint trails off to the right for about 200 yards into the woods.

ma_house_rock.blurb: A very large glacial erratic standing in a small town park in Weymouth, south of Boston, at the end of a residential street. The block is around 30 feet tall and offers short trad and top-rope lines, including a well-liked 5.8 hand crack, plus a set of boulder problems. Trad and top-rope climbs range from 5.5 up to the 5.10 range, while the boulder problems stretch from easy to very hard. The setting is a playground and picnic park rather than a wilderness crag, so expect other visitors, and bring a pad for the problems.
ma_house_rock.parking_note: Park at the end of House Rock Road in Weymouth; space is limited to roughly four cars.
